title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock or ETF in Stage 4, no matter how cheap it looks; a falling 30-week moving average is a ceiling of trapped supply, not a bargain basement.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets

web_blocks.html: On November 20, 2026, KORU sits deep inside a confirmed Stage 4 (Markdown) downtrend across both our market-facts ledger (stage: 4) and TradingView snapshot (STAGE_4, CAP_REJECTED) [26]. Closing at $4.76 after a -25.04% single-day flush, KORU trades -80.64% below its 30-week SMA ($24.59), -80.00% below its 200-day SMA ($23.80), and -66.38% below its 50-day SMA ($14.16) [26]. It also sits -60.27% below its TradingView 10-week EMA ($11.98) and -62.99% below its facts-ledger 10W EMA approximation ($12.86). Most critically, the $4.76 close breached the prior $5.22 structural invalidation stop.

Both the underlying Korean benchmark and the broader US market confirm systemic distribution. Unleveraged EWY ($123.26) dropped -8.42% on the day into confirmed STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED), sitting -29.32% below its 30-week SMA ($174.38) and -24.37% below its 50-day SMA ($162.97) [27]. Meanwhile, the US market regime stands in an official Downtrend: S&P 500 breadth is just 38.8% above the 50-DMA and 46.9% above the 200-DMA, with 10 distribution days logged over the past 25 sessions. Only 3 of 11 S&P sectors remain above their 50-day moving averages.

web_blocks.html: Re-entering KORU onto any future watchlist requires strict multi-step confirmation. First, unleveraged EWY ($123.26) must exit Stage 4, build a flat Stage 1 base, and reclaim its 30-week SMA ($174.38) [27]. Second, KORU must stop making lower lows beneath $4.59, reclaim its $11.80–$14.37 screen band (10W EMA $11.98 and 50D SMA $14.16) on 1.5x+ accumulation volume, and see daily ATR shrink well below 29% of price. Until then, catching a 29.77-RSI bounce in a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend is pure speculation.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 gave you the mathematical reason why KORU can lose money even in an up year for Korean equities, Chapter 8 reads the November 20, 2026 tape to show how decisively the market has voted. Pull up the weekly, daily, and 4-hour charts of AMEX:KORU, and there is no ambiguity whatsoever. Both our market-facts ledger and our TradingView snapshot classify KORU in Stage 4 markdown—and the technical timing gate is hard CAP_REJECTED.

At Friday's close of $4.76, following a brutal -25.04% single-day collapse on 93.41 million shares (1.80 times 20-day average volume), KORU is down -38.02% in a single week and -92.56% from its $63.99 52-week high. Look at the moving averages stacked overhead: the 10-day SMA sits at $7.02, the 20-day SMA at $8.77, the 10-week EMA at $11.98 ($12.86 in the facts approximation), the 50-day SMA at $14.16, the 200-day SMA at $23.80, and the 30-week SMA at $24.59. Every single trendline is sloping downward far above current price—at -66.38% below the 50-day and -80.64% below the 30-week average.

Zooming in to the 4-hour intraday chart confirms there is no hidden turn forming beneath the surface. The 4-hour 20-EMA sits at $7.03 and the 4-hour 50-SMA sits at $9.29, while the 4-hour RSI has fallen to 26.54 and our intraday turn flag reads false. Daily RSI sits at 29.77 and weekly RSI sits at 36.18. Yes, an RSI under 30 signals short-term oversold conditions—but in a Stage 4 crash with a 14-day Average True Range of $1.39 (nearly 30% of the entire share price) and Bollinger Band width stretched to 204.41%, oversold readings can easily become deeply oversold before any durable floor forms.

Crucially, Friday's slide to $4.76 also shattered two critical technical shelves. It broke cleanly beneath our prior $5.22 structural invalidation stop—triggering a mandatory stop-breach exit rule—and fell below TradingView's Pivot S1 at $5.99. The only nearby reference floor left is the $4.59 52-week low, sitting just 3.6% below Friday's close. If $4.59 gives way next week, the chart shows an air pocket straight toward Pivot S2 at $1.34—the exact sub-$2 price neighborhood that forces Direxion to schedule another 1-for-10 reverse split.

What about the broader ecosystem? Look at unleveraged EWY at $123.26, down -8.42% on Friday and -22.22% over the past month. EWY has now fallen -29.32% below its $174.38 30-week SMA and -24.37% below its $162.97 50-day SMA, placing EWY itself in confirmed Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED). Meanwhile, the US market regime has deteriorated from a Correction into a full Downtrend: only 38.8% of S&P stocks hold above their 50-day moving averages, 46.9% hold above their 200-day averages, and institutions have printed 10 distribution days over the past 25 sessions. When both Seoul and Wall Street are under heavy institutional distribution, an 8.35-beta leveraged ETF is the last asset you want to own.

Finally, our options desk package confirms NO_OPTIONS_EDGE on KORU. With price buried beneath both the 50-day and 200-day structural floors and fundamentals rated CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rather than COMPOUNDER_PASS, every call or call-spread strategy fails our quality gate. The tape speaks with one voice: stand completely aside.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a 3x ETF drops 25% in a single session on 1.8x volume to hit a 29.77 RSI, the temptation is to say 'it is too late to sell now.' Stan Weinstein's rule exists for that exact moment: breaking a $5.22 stop in Stage 4 is not a time to hope for a bounce; it is the market demanding you respect your exit rule before $4.59 gives way toward $1.34.

section_takeaway: KORU ($4.76) breached its $5.22 prior stop in Stage 4 (-80.64% vs 30W SMA), EWY ($123.26) sits in Stage 4, the US market is in a Downtrend (10 dist. days), and options carry NO_OPTIONS_EDGE.

book_subsections.title: 8.1 Multi-Timeframe Anatomy: Why $4.76 Is Broken Across 1W, 1D, and 4H
paragraphs: Whether you examine the weekly, daily, or 4-hour timeframe, KORU displays textbook Stage 4 liquidation. On the weekly chart, price at $4.76 sits -80.64% below the declining 30-week SMA ($24.59). On the daily chart, price sits -66.38% below the 50-day SMA ($14.16) and -80.00% below the 200-day SMA ($23.80). Even on the 4-hour chart, price remains pinned far below the 20-EMA ($7.03) and 50-SMA ($9.29) with zero upward turn.

Notice what the TradingView screen's $11.80–$14.37 support band actually represents right now. Because KORU crashed straight through prior support, that $11.80–$14.37 zone—centered on the 10-week EMA ($11.98) and 50-day SMA ($14.16)—is now overhead reclaim territory, more than +148% above current price. There is no active buy zone below $4.76.

book_subsections.title: 8.2 Stop Breach ($4.76 <= $5.22) and the $4.59 Cliff
paragraphs: Risk management works only if stops are honored when violated. In our prior review, KORU's structural invalidation stop stood at $5.22. Friday's -25.04% plunge to $4.76 sliced directly through $5.22 on 93.41 million shares—leaving no ambiguity that the stop has been breached.

With the 52-week low sitting at $4.59 just seventeen cents below Friday's close, waiting for an arbitrary bounce exposes remaining capital to a gap toward Pivot S2 at $1.34. And remember that when daily ATR equals $1.39—29.2% of the stock's price—a routine two-day downdraft can erase another 40% to 50% of account equity before a limit order fills.

book_subsections.title: 8.3 Why EWY's Stage 4 and the US Downtrend Veto Bottom-Fishing
paragraphs: In Stage Analysis, you never try to catch a falling leveraged ETF when its underlying index and the broad market are both breaking down. Unleveraged EWY fell -8.42% on Friday to $123.26, trading -29.32% below its 30-week SMA ($174.38) and -24.37% below its 50-day SMA ($162.97) on 1.79x average volume. That puts EWY firmly in Stage 4.

At the same time, the S&P 500 sits in an official Downtrend with 10 distribution days in 25 sessions and only 38.8% of breadth above the 50-DMA. Institutional portfolios are actively de-risking, not rotating into 8.35-beta Korean semiconductors.

book_subsections.title: 8.4 Options Desk Stance: Why NO_OPTIONS_EDGE Means Zero Spreads
paragraphs: Some traders look at an oversold RSI of 29.77 and hunt for cheap out-of-the-money call spreads as lottery tickets. Our November 20, 2026 options package explicitly assigns NO_OPTIONS_EDGE to KORU. With price below every major daily and weekly moving average and the fund lacking a COMPOUNDER_PASS quality rating, options premium decays rapidly against falling prices and wide bid-ask spreads. Do not place any options trade on KORU.

book_subsections.title: 8.5 Reading the Complete Price Ladder from $63.99 Down to $4.76
paragraphs: Look at the structural map from top to bottom as of November 20, 2026. KORU peaked at $63.99 over the trailing 52 weeks before sliding -92.56% to $4.76. Between Friday's $4.76 close and the 30-week moving average at $24.59 sit six distinct layers of trapped overhead supply: the broken $5.22 prior stop and $5.99 Pivot S1 shelf, the 10-day SMA at $7.02, the 20-day SMA at $8.77, the 10-week EMA at $11.98, the 50-day SMA at $14.16, and the 200-day SMA at $23.80.

On the downside, the only nearby reference level is the 52-week low at $4.59—barely seventeen cents below Friday's close. If $4.59 breaks on heavy volume next week, the chart opens straight down toward Pivot S2 at $1.34. When reward-to-risk is upside-down across weekly, daily, and 4-hour timeframes, stepping out of the way is the only rational move.

book_subsections.title: 8.6 Exact Technical Prerequisites Before Ever Revisiting South Korea
paragraphs: Nothing stays in Stage 4 forever, so write down the exact objective checklist that would put South Korean equities back on a future watchlist. First, the S&P 500 must exit its 10-distribution-day Downtrend and push breadth back above 50% over the 50-day moving average. Second, unleveraged EWY ($123.26) must stop making lower lows, carve a multi-week horizontal Stage 1 base, and reclaim its rising 30-week SMA ($174.38).

Third, realized index volatility must cool from the current 60%–65% range down below 30% annualized so daily compounding stops eating capital. Until every single one of those conditions is visible in hard data, patience costs nothing while premature bottom-fishing risks permanent impairment.

book_subsections.title: 8.7 Comparing KORU's Volume Surge Against Institutional Accumulation Rules
paragraphs: Beginners often mistake a high-volume drop near a 52-week low for institutional bargain hunting. Friday's tape proves the difference. On November 20, 2026, KORU traded 93.41 million shares—1.80 times its 20-day average—while plunging -25.04% to $4.76. Over the trailing 25 sessions, the fund logged nine distribution days.

True institutional accumulation looks completely different. In a valid Stage 1 base, price stops falling, holds flat for weeks inside a tight range, and then surges above its 10-week EMA and 50-day SMA on expanding up-day volume. Until KORU reclaims its $11.80–$14.37 band on strong accumulation, high volume on down days confirms forced liquidation rather than support.
